books.section: Topic 7.4 The Progressives — Progressivism and Woodrow Wilson
The Progressive Era and World War I (1900-1920)

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of 5 Steps to a 5 2024, Chapter 20, and Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of 5 Steps to a 5 2024, Chapter 20, and Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9: Woodrow Wilson won in 1912 on his New Freedom program. In 1913 he cut tariffs with the Underwood Tariff Act and signed the Federal Reserve Act, creating a central banking system of twelve regional banks to steady credit and the currency. The Sixteenth Amendment, ratified in 1913, let Congress collect an income tax. In 1914 the Clayton Antitrust Act outlawed price discrimination and exempted labor unions from antitrust prosecution, and the Federal Trade Commission Act created a commission to police unfair business practices.

stem: The Clayton Antitrust Act of 1914 was a victory for organized labor because it

options.misconception: The act did the opposite: it exempted unions from antitrust prosecution.

options.text: set a national minimum wage for all American workers
options.misconception: A national minimum wage came later, in the 1930s; the Clayton Act was about antitrust and union rights.

options.text: outlawed the eight-hour day for factory workers
options.misconception: The act legalized strikes and boycotts; it did not outlaw shorter hours, which reformers were demanding.

options.text: exempted unions from antitrust prosecution and legalized strikes and boycotts

rationales.A: The Clayton Act protected unions from antitrust law. Banning them would reverse its purpose.
rationales.B: No minimum wage appears in the Clayton Act. That reform belonged to the New Deal era.
rationales.C: The act moved toward labor's goals, not against them. It legalized strikes and boycotts rather than banning shorter hours.
rationales.D: The Sherman Act had been used against unions, as in the Danbury Hatters case. The Clayton Act exempted unions from antitrust prosecution and legalized strikes and boycotts, which is why Samuel Gompers called it labor's Magna Carta.
rationales.general:
1. Recall the old problem. The Sherman Act, written against trusts, had been turned against unions.
2. Read the fix. The Clayton Act exempted unions from antitrust prosecution and legalized strikes and boycotts.
3. Rule out the reversals. Banning unions, setting wages, and outlawing shorter hours all point the wrong way.
Remember: a law helps labor when it takes away the weapon used against labor, so ask what the old law did to unions first.
